Job Summary

  • Understand, acknowledge and comply with the requirements on individual accountabilities and responsibilities of the job set out in applicable local laws and regulations as well as SCB internal policies;

理解、认同并遵守本地法律法规以及渣打内部政策中关于个人问责和职责的要求；

  • Effectively ensure and intensify internal controls by keeping abreast with developments of applicable local laws and regulations on accountabilities;

跟上本地问责法律法规的发展，以有效地确保并强化内控；

  • Perform job duties with diligence, contribute to efforts as an individual or as a team member so as to avoid any actual or potential legal sanctions, regulatory penalties, material financial loss, or adverse reputational impact on the Bank;

审慎勤勉地履行岗位职责，以个人或团队成员的身份，为避免任何导致银行遭受或可能遭受法律制裁、监管处罚、重大财务损失或声誉负面影响而做出努力；

  • Be responsible for failure to follow relevant rules and processes, failure to properly perform the responsibilities, and implement corrections;

对未遵守相关规范和流程、未适当履行职责以及未执行整改措施承担相应责任；

  • Cooperate with any investigations or reviews on regulatory failure such as accountability review.

配合任何关于违反监管规定的调查或审查，例如，问责审查。

Key Responsibilities

Strategy

  • Coverage of CMPS products (structured products) to deliver the proper solutions under the framework of Business Strategy to meet the needs across from Retail Banking and Business Banking clients.

覆盖资本市场产品及解决方案部的产品（结构性产品），在业务战略框架下提供适当的解决方案，以满足零售银行和中小企业银行客户的需求。

  • Manage and develop strong product solutions and smooth workflow to deliver differentiated product proposition and brand identity. 开发并管理强大的产品解决方案和顺畅的工作流程；提供独特的产品主张和品牌标识。
  • To develop and manage the full range of structured products with reference to the overall Wealth Solution Strategy.
  • Manage and maintain the development of the strong and differentiated product proposition and brand identity.

Business

  • Product pipeline planning产品受众规划
  • Provision of best execution for CMPS products资本市场产品及解决方案部的产品的最佳执行

  • Deliver new products to market to grow customer base and revenue
  • Collaborate with key country stakeholders in Wealth Management, Retail Banking, Technology and Operations to deliver the best value to our customers

持续关注市场变化和行业趋势，力争产品创新。

与其他团队进行专业地合作和沟通。

  • Mitigation of risks and resolution of issues in a timely manner including developing suitable controls and measuring their effectiveness.

制定适当的风险控制措施并衡量其有效性，缓解风险，解决问题。

  • Proactive identification and reporting of risks and concerns.

主动识别和报告风险问题

  • Adherence to laws and regulations, internal risk and compliance policies (including anti-money laundry, sanction, anti-bribery & corruption and relevant FCC risks) and the Group Code of Conduct.

及时完成所有风险和合规强制性培训，包括在规定的截止日期前进行e-learning课程。

充分理解消费者权益保护的重要性，防止损害消费者的最佳利益，执行与消费者权益保护相关的监管要求，确保完成相关培训，并在日常工作中始终嵌入消费者权益保护意识。

充分认识防欺诈的重要性，防范欺诈风险，维护岗位安全稳定运行，落实防欺诈监管要求，严格执行部门管理文件，确保完成相关培训，将防欺诈融入日常工作。

About Standard Chartered

We're an international bank, nimble enough to act, big enough for impact. For more than 170 years, we've worked to make a positive difference for our clients, communities, and each other. We question the status quo, love a challenge and enjoy finding new opportunities to grow and do better than before. If you're looking for a career with purpose and you want to work for a bank making a difference, we want to hear from you. You can count on us to celebrate your unique talents and we can't wait to see the talents you can bring us.

Our purpose, to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, together with our brand promise, to be here for good are achieved by how we each live our valued behaviours. When you work with us, you'll see how we value difference and advocate inclusion.

Together We

  • Do the right thing and are assertive, challenge one another, and live with integrity, while putting the client at the heart of what we do
  • Never settle, continuously striving to improve and innovate, keeping things simple and learning from doing well, and not so well
  • Are better together, we can be ourselves, be inclusive, see more good in others, and work collectively to build for the long term

What We Offer

In line with our Fair Pay Charter, we offer a competitive salary and benefits to support your mental, physical, financial and social wellbeing.

  • Core bank funding for retirement savings, medical and life insurance, with flexible and voluntary benefits available in some locations.
  • Time-off including annual leave, parental/maternity (20 weeks), sabbatical (12 months maximum) and volunteering leave (3 days), along with minimum global standards for annual and public holiday, which is combined to 30 days minimum.
  • Flexible working options based around home and office locations, with flexible working patterns.
  • Proactive wellbeing support through Unmind, a market-leading digital wellbeing platform, development courses for resilience and other human skills, global Employee Assistance Programme, sick leave, mental health first-aiders and all sorts of self-help toolkits
  • A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual and digital learning.
  • Being part of an inclusive and values driven organisation, one that embraces and celebrates our unique diversity, across our teams, business functions and geographies - everyone feels respected and can realise their full potential.

Some Careers Have More Impact Than Others.

If you’re looking for a career where you can make a real impression, join HSBC and discover how valued you’ll be.

We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team in the role of Associate Director, Software Engineering Specialist.

Business: Group Functions Technology L3

Principal Responsibilities

  • Lead technical design discussions, document decisions and trade-offs, mentor engineers, and provide hands-on code reviews while working closely with architecture, data, platform, security, and product teams.
  • Integrate LLM/GenAI capabilities (e.g., RAG, prompt/agent patterns) into business workflows, ensuring outputs are reproducible, testable, explainable where required, and suitable for audit/review.
  • Design, build, test, and operate scalable, reliable backend services and APIs (primarily Python/FastAPI), evolving a proof of concept into a secure production capability.
  • Define stable API contracts and integration patterns for internal/external consumers, with clear versioning, documentation, and backwards-compatibility where required.
  • Create clean technical boundaries between product-specific functionality and reusable platform capabilities to enable reuse across multiple consumers.
  • Design and implement data ingestion and integration pipelines to validate, transform, enrich, and publish domain data using batch and event-driven patterns.
  • Implement pipeline controls for data quality, reconciliation, idempotency, retries, error handling, recovery, lineage, metadata, and provenance.
  • Build and maintain knowledge/retrieval capabilities over domain data (e.g., metadata/semantic models, knowledge graphs or equivalent), enabling trusted querying and interpretation.
  • Embed production engineering practices: automated testing (unit/integration/contract/E2E), observability (logs/metrics/traces/alerts/dashboards), resilience, secrets/configuration management, and incident/problem resolution.
  • Significant senior backend engineering experience delivering and operating production services.
  • Strong Python skills and experience with modern API frameworks such as FastAPI; strong REST API design including contract design and versioning.
  • Hands-on experience integrating GenAI/LLMs into applications (e.g., RAG, retrieval, prompt lifecycle management, evaluation/quality assurance) and familiarity with knowledge modelling (knowledge graphs/ontologies/semantic models) or equivalent approaches.
  • Solid distributed-systems fundamentals and service integration patterns (sync/async), with experience building reusable modules/capabilities.
  • Strong relational database and SQL skills: data modelling, schema migrations, and query performance tuning; experience handling structured and semi-structured data.
  • Proven experience designing and building data pipelines (batch and/or event-driven), including orchestration/scheduling, retries, idempotency, validation, and recovery.
  • Strong understanding of data quality and trust controls: reconciliation, data contracts, schema evolution, lineage, metadata, and provenance.
  • Cloud-native engineering experience: containers, Kubernetes, and CI/CD; ability to integrate with platform/infrastructure services.
  • Security engineering experience: authentication/authorization, secure service-to-service communication, secrets handling, and secure handling of sensitive data.
  • Production ownership mindset with strong observability and support practices (logging, metrics, tracing, alerting, incident investigation).
  • Comfortable leading design discussions, communicating trade-offs clearly, and working collaboratively across engineering, architecture, data, security, and platform teams in a regulated environment.

You’ll achieve more when you join HSBC.

HSBC is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a culture where all employees are valued, respected and opinions count. We take pride in providing a workplace that fosters continuous professional development, flexible working and, opportunities to grow within an inclusive and diverse environment. We encourage applications from all suitably qualified persons irrespective of, but not limited to, their gender or genetic information, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, social status, medical care leave requirements, political affiliation, people with disabilities, color, national origin, veteran status, etc., We consider all applications based on merit and suitability to the role.

Personal data held by the Bank relating to employment applications will be used in accordance with our Privacy Statement, which is available on our website.

***Issued By HSBC Software Development (GuangDong) Limited***

Coverage Banking Internship Programme 2027

Join our Coverage Banking team and gain first-hand experience supporting some of the world’s leading corporates, financial institutions, investors and public sector clients. As part of the client-facing arm of Corporate & Investment Banking (CIB), you’ll work alongside experienced bankers to help deliver integrated banking solutions, build client relationships and support strategic growth opportunities across markets.

With our unique international footprint, you’ll gain exposure to cross-border business, global clients and real-world banking challenges. You’ll work across teams, products and geographies while developing the commercial, analytical and relationship-building skills that underpin a successful career in banking.

Join us if you’re curious about how businesses grow, how financial markets operate and how trusted client relationships are built.

About the Internship Programme – how you’ll learn and grow 

Join a skills-first organisation where your potential matters more than your background. Over 10 weeks, you’ll work on real business challenges, build future-ready skills, and gain insight into how we support clients, facilitate trade and finance growth across our markets. Working alongside colleagues across our global network, you’ll develop the skills, confidence and connections to accelerate your career. For many interns, this is the first step towards a graduate role with us.

The Programme Will Support Your Development Through

  • A 10-week summer internship 
  • A structured induction and orientation 
  • Exposure to our products, clients and international network
  • Real projects and meaningful responsibilities from day one
  • Technical, professional and behavioural skills development
  • Support from managers, mentors and buddies
  • Opportunities to learn from senior leaders and industry experts
  • Community and volunteering initiatives.

Where you could work

You will be placed into one of the following Coverage Banking teams, working alongside experienced bankers to support client relationships, business development activities and transaction execution across our global franchise.

  • Corporate Coverage: Support relationship teams managing multinational corporations, large local corporates and mid-market clients. You’ll gain exposure to financing solutions, transaction banking, capital markets activities and strategic client engagement while learning how long-term client relationships are developed and managed.
  • Financial Institutions Coverage: Work with teams covering banks, insurance companies, asset managers, sovereign entities and other financial institutions. You’ll gain insight into how financial institutions access financing, manage risk and utilise the Bank’s global capabilities to support their businesses.
  • Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A): Gain exposure to landmark transactions including acquisitions, divestments, mergers and strategic partnerships. You’ll support research, analysis and deal execution activities while learning how clients navigate transformational business decisions.

Bring the skills - we’ll help you build your career

We welcome students from all degree disciplines and backgrounds, recognising that diverse perspectives drive innovation.

We’re Looking For People Who Can

  • Take ownership and show initiative.
  • Think critically and solve problems using logic and sound judgement.
  • Learn quickly, stay curious and seek opportunities to grow.
  • Build strong relationships and collaborate effectively with others.
  • Adapt and perform in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrate commercial curiosity and an interest in clients, industries and global markets.
  • Communicate confidently and work effectively across different cultures and backgrounds.

Eligibility   

To be eligible for this internship, you should be a penultimate year student, able to intern in June 2027, and start full time in July 2028. You should have the permanent legal right to work in the country you’re applying to.   

You can only submit one application within a six-month period, so take time to review our opportunities and apply for the role that best fits your interests, skills and career goals.

Key Dates

  • Assessment Centres: October 2026 onwards
  • Start Date: June 2027

About Corporate & Investment Banking (CIB) 

We are a super-connector for many of the world’s largest companies across more than 50 markets, playing a central role in global trade, capital flows and economic growth. We work with governments, financial institutions, and some of the world’s most ambitious corporates to help them expand, invest, and navigate uncertainty across increasingly complex and fast-changing markets.

What makes us distinctive is our combination of deep local expertise with an extensive and unique global network. We support clients across risk management, financing, transaction services, advisory, and sustainable finance, helping move capital to where it’s needed most and supporting the real economy across our footprint.

About Standard Chartered

We're an international bank, nimble enough to act, big enough for impact. For more than 170 years, we've worked to make a positive difference for our clients, communities, and each other. We question the status quo, love a challenge and enjoy finding new opportunities to grow and do better than before. If you're looking for a career with purpose and you want to work for a bank making a difference, we want to hear from you. You can count on us to celebrate your unique talents and we can't wait to see the talents you can bring us.

Our purpose, to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, together with our brand promise, to be here for good are achieved by how we each live our valued behaviours. When you work with us, you'll see how we value difference and advocate inclusion.

Together We

  • Do the right thing and are assertive, challenge one another, and live with integrity, while putting the client at the heart of what we do
  • Never settle, continuously striving to improve and innovate, keeping things simple and learning from doing well, and not so well
  • Are better together, we can be ourselves, be inclusive, see more good in others, and work collectively to build for the long term

What we offer

In line with our Fair Pay Charter, we offer a competitive salary and benefits to support your mental, physical, financial and social wellbeing.

  • Core bank funding for retirement savings, medical and life insurance, with flexible and voluntary benefits available in some locations.
  • Time-off including annual leave, parental/maternity (20 weeks), sabbatical (12 months maximum) and volunteering leave (3 days), along with minimum global standards for annual and public holiday, which is combined to 30 days minimum.
  • Flexible working options based around home and office locations, with flexible working patterns.
  • Proactive wellbeing support through Unmind, a market-leading digital wellbeing platform, development courses for resilience and other human skills, global Employee Assistance Programme, sick leave, mental health first-aiders and all sorts of self-help toolkits
  • A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual and digital learning.
  • Being part of an inclusive and values driven organisation, one that embraces and celebrates our unique diversity, across our teams, business functions and geographies - everyone feels respected and can realise their full potential.

Recruitment Assessments

Some of our roles use assessments to help us understand how suitable you are for the role you've applied to. If you are invited to take an assessment, this is great news. It means your application has progressed to an important stage of our recruitment process.

Visit our careers website www.sc.com/careers

Job Description

Join our team to play a pivotal role in mitigating tech risks and upholding operational excellence, driving innovation in risk management.

As a Tech Risk & Controls Lead, you will be responsible for identifying, and mitigating compliance and operational risks in line with the firm's standards. You will also provide subject matter expertise and technical guidance to technology-aligned process owners, ensuring that implemented controls are operating effectively and in compliance with regulatory, legal, and industry standards. By partnering with various stakeholders, including Product Owners, Business Control Managers, and Regulators, you will contribute to the reporting of a comprehensive view of technology risk posture and its impact on the business. Your advanced knowledge of risk management principles, practices, and theories will enable you to drive innovative solutions and effectively manage a diverse team in a dynamic and evolving risk landscape.

Job Responsibilities

  • Ensure effective identification, quantification, communication, and management of technology risk, focusing on root cause analysis and resolution recommendations
  • Develop and maintain robust relationships, becoming a trusted partner with LOB technologists, assessments teams, and data officers to facilitate cross-functional collaboration and progress toward shared goals
  • Leverages tools and emerging technology to lead the execution of technical risk assessments at a large scale across the Asia Pacific technology estate of ‘last mile' applications and in-country applications
  • Guides the evaluation of current cybersecurity principals, processes, and controls, and leads the evaluation of new technology using existing standards and frameworks
  • Execute reporting and governance of controls, policies, issue management, and measurements, offering senior management insights into control effectiveness and inform governance work
  • Proactively monitor and evaluate control effectiveness, identify gaps, and recommend enhancements to strengthen risk posture and regulatory compliance

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills

  • 5+ years of experience or equivalent expertise in technology risk management, information security, or related field, emphasizing risk identification, assessment, and mitigation
  • Hands-on practical experience delivering enterprise level cybersecurity solutions and controls
  • Familiarity with risk management frameworks, industry standards, and financial industry regulatory requirements
  • Proficient knowledge and expertise in cybersecurity architecture, applications, data security, risk assessment & reporting, control evaluation, design, and governance, with a proven record of implementing effective risk mitigation strategies
  • Demonstrated ability to influence executive-level strategic decision-making and translating technology insights into business strategies for senior executives

Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills

  • CISM, CRISC, CISSP, or similar industry-recognized risk and risk certifications are preferred

ABOUT US

J.P. Morgan is a global leader in financial services, providing strategic advice and products to the world's most prominent corporations, governments, wealthy individuals and institutional investors. Our first-class business in a first-class way approach to serving clients drives everything we do. We strive to build trusted, long-term partnerships to help our clients achieve their business objectives.

We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation.

About The Team

Our professionals in our Corporate Functions cover a diverse range of areas from finance and risk to human resources and marketing. Our corporate teams are an essential part of our company, ensuring that we're setting our businesses, clients, customers and employees up for success.

The RAM is responsible for establishing and maintaining an end to end understanding of the client structure, client needs and steering the client relationship through Account Planning. The RAM shall work closely with the GS Head and will be responsible to embrace our corridor engagement on country perspective and hold accountabilities to drive regional revenues.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy

  • Responsible for delivery of agreed business performance targets (Revenue, RoRWA, RWA, costs, etc.) for the designated portfolio.

Business

  • Be responsible for significant losses due to failure of effectiveness of internal control

  • Credit knowledge
  • Compliance, Risk and Governance Management

Qualifications

  • Awareness of the market landscape (China)
  • Previous experience in managing C Suite and regional treasurers
  • Deep understanding of client’s business model and identify business opportunities.
  • Thorough understanding of Risk (Credit, Operational and Fraud Risk) incl passing all the internal required tests/ eLearnings
  • Product knowledge and previous experience with complex transactions
  • Softer skills of managing clients across diverse cultures
  • Understand and good adapt of garnering cultural sensitivities
  • Deliver strategic workstream

We're an international bank, nimble enough to act, big enough for impact. For more than 170 years, we've worked to make a positive difference for our clients, communities, and each other. We question the status quo, love a challenge and enjoy finding new opportunities to grow and do better than before. If you're looking for a career with purpose and you want to work for a bank making a difference, we want to hear from you. You can count on us to celebrate your unique talents and we can't wait to see the talents you can bring us.

Our purpose, to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, together with our brand promise, to be here for good are achieved by how we each live our valued behaviours. When you work with us, you'll see how we value difference and advocate inclusion.

Together We

  • Do the right thing and are assertive, challenge one another, and live with integrity, while putting the client at the heart of what we do
  • Never settle, continuously striving to improve and innovate, keeping things simple and learning from doing well, and not so well
  • Are better together, we can be ourselves, be inclusive, see more good in others, and work collectively to build for the long term

What We Offer

In line with our Fair Pay Charter, we offer a competitive salary and benefits to support your mental, physical, financial and social wellbeing.

  • Core bank funding for retirement savings, medical and life insurance, with flexible and voluntary benefits available in some locations.
  • Time-off including annual leave, parental/maternity (20 weeks), sabbatical (12 months maximum) and volunteering leave (3 days), along with minimum global standards for annual and public holiday, which is combined to 30 days minimum.
  • Flexible working options based around home and office locations, with flexible working patterns.
  • Proactive wellbeing support through Unmind, a market-leading digital wellbeing platform, development courses for resilience and other human skills, global Employee Assistance Programme, sick leave, mental health first-aiders and all sorts of self-help toolkits
  • A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual and digital learning.
  • Being part of an inclusive and values driven organisation, one that embraces and celebrates our unique diversity, across our teams, business functions and geographies - everyone feels respected and can realise their full potential.

Ready to shape Corporate Sales growth for Strategic and Focus clients?

Why HSBC

HSBC is one of the largest banking and financial services organisations in the world. Guided by our purpose of opening up a world of opportunity, our ambition is to become the world’s most trusted bank globally, putting customers at the heart of everything we do.

The Role

Corporate Sales sits within HSBC Corporate and Institutional Banking (CIB) and supports corporate clients with relevant products, solutions and market insight. This role focuses on serving Strategic and Focus clients, building trusted relationships and improving product penetration and wallet share. You’ll manage revenue and profitability across an allocated client portfolio while delivering a high standard of service from idea through to execution and post-trade. The role also has a strong focus on improving the cost of service delivery including shifting transactional activity towards e-capability where appropriate. Where supervisory responsibilities apply, you’ll set direction for the local Corporate Sales team and maintain a strong control environment across front office activity. Success means measurable portfolio growth, strong client feedback and consistent delivery in line with HSBC policies and regulatory expectations.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Manage a portfolio of Strategic and Focus corporate clients with clear ownership of revenue performance
  • Identify sales opportunities end-to-end from client need through execution and post-trade support
  • Provide day-to-day coverage across the Corporate Sales offering, coordinating with trading teams to support execution flow
  • Develop client relationships that strengthen product penetration and expand share of wallet across priority accounts
  • Partner with Relationship Managers, Global Payments Solutions (GPS) and Global Trade Solutions (GTS) to meet client needs
  • Champion adoption of appropriate service models such as migrating transactional activity to self-service e-capability
  • Coordinate with Corporate Risk Solutions (CRS) for complex balance sheet structuring solutions and cross-sell opportunities
  • Maintain an effective control environment, escalating unusual or unacceptable activity and supporting fair customer outcomes
  • Oversee team activity where supervisory responsibilities apply including performance management, coaching and resource planning
  • Adapt processes as technology platforms evolve while keeping service quality and risk controls front of mind

What We're Looking For

  • Bring strong experience in Corporate Sales including knowledge of products, clients, systems and key processes
  • Apply established understanding of capital markets including foreign exchange instruments and interest rate derivatives
  • Manage transaction flow from order through to execution in partnership with trading teams and internal stakeholders
  • Demonstrate a track record of developing client relationships that translate into revenue growth and deeper product usage
  • Partner effectively across teams and regions to deliver coordinated client coverage and consistent service
  • Operate within regulatory requirements for non-advisory sales and trading activities including holding relevant local or cross-border exams and qualifications or equivalent demonstrable experience
  • Apply sound judgement in managing conduct risk, financial crime risk and operational risk within a front office environment
  • Supervise and develop team members where applicable including performance management, coaching and maintaining quality of output

Building deeper Corporate Sales relationships

This role offers the chance to shape how HSBC supports Strategic and Focus corporate clients across products, execution and service models. You’ll be central to improving client outcomes while strengthening revenue performance and operational efficiency. Where supervisory responsibilities apply, you’ll also create clarity on standards and controls and support a consistent approach to front office supervision.

If you want your work to be measured in client trust, disciplined execution and sustainable growth this role is a strong platform to build from. Apply to help expand the HSBC Corporate Sales franchise through relationships that last and solutions that land well in market.

Recognized technical authority for an area within the business. Requires basic commercial awareness.   • Sell separate account services or finance products directly to Corporate clients
  • Will help team to service clients in the buying and selling of securities, derivatives, FX and commodities
  • Help drive the team's developed strategy across specified product lines
  • Aid to achieve specified goals in both market and wallet share for the identified client franchise
  • Originate and execute meaningful and landmark transactions
  • Will independently and/or jointly work within business product to achieve the strategic growth and market share we are aiming for
  • Partner closely with other key businesses and functions to ensure proper product deployment based on understanding of client

  • Appropriately assess risk/reward of transactions when making business decisions; demonstrating proper consideration for the firm’s reputation.

  • Appropriately assess risk when business decisions are made, demonstrating particular consideration for the firm's reputation and safeguarding Citigroup, its clients and assets, by driving compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, adhering to Policy, applying sound ethical judgment regarding personal behavior, conduct and business practices, and escalating, managing and reporting control issues with transparency.
